author: Ian Johnson
name: Hardened Function
description: A Hardened serverless function: a handler bound to a provider-neutral trigger, its services, and a test project that runs it without a cloud.

trigger.description: What reaches the handler. The attribute is provider-neutral: which adapter serves it is decided by --host, not by the handler.

choices.description: A direct invocation. The payload is the handler's parameter and its return value is the response. On AWS, a Lambda invoked by an SDK caller, Step Functions or a test.
Messages off a queue, delivered as a batch and handled one at a time. SQS on AWS, Service Bus on Azure, Pub/Sub on Google.
Notifications published to a topic. SNS on AWS, Service Bus topics on Azure, Pub/Sub on Google.
A schedule. EventBridge Scheduler on AWS, a timer trigger on Azure, Cloud Scheduler on Google.
Changes to a table's rows, in order and replayable. DynamoDB Streams on AWS, the Cosmos DB change feed on Azure, Firestore triggers on Google.
Records off a sharded stream, in order and replayable. Kinesis Data Streams on AWS, Event Hubs on Azure.
Objects changing in a store. The notification is the message and the object is not in it. S3 on AWS, Blob Storage on Azure, Cloud Storage on Google.

host.description: Which cloud runs the function. The handler does not change with it - the host decides one package reference and the entry point.

choices.description: AWS Lambda. The only host with adapters today; Azure and Google are the reason this is a flag rather than the premise.

HardenedVersion.description: The Hardened package version to pin. Defaults to the version this template shipped with.

skipRestore.description: Skip the automatic restore after creation.

testFramework.description: The test framework the test project runs on. [HardenedTest] reads the same on either; the runner package and the assertion style are what change.

mocks.description: The library a [Mock] parameter's double comes from: one package and one assembly attribute in the test project. [Mock] itself is the same.

choices.description: Moq. A Mock<T> parameter is the mock to configure; [Mock] T is the object it produces.

postActions.description: Restore the packages the template pinned.
